questions.title: An exponential transformation on a finite interval
questions.prompt_html:
The density of \(X\) is

\[f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac3{20}\left(e^{x/2}+2e^{-x/2}\right),&0\le x\le2\ln3,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

  1. Find the cumulative distribution function of \(X\).

    [3]

  2. Let \(Y=e^{X/2}\). Find the probability density function of \(Y\).

    [3]

  3. Find the 60th percentile of \(Y\).

    [2]

  4. Find \(\mathrm E(Y^4)\).

    [3]
questions.answer_html:
(a)

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 0\\\frac3{10}\left(e^{x/2}-2e^{-x/2}+1\right),&0\le x\lt 2 \ln{\left(3 \right)}\\1,&x\ge 2 \ln{\left(3 \right)}.\end{cases}\]

(b)

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{3 \left(1 + \frac{2}{y^{2}}\right)}{10},&1\le y\le 3\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

(c)

\[2.\]

(d)

\[\frac{493}{25}.\]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

For \(0\le x\le2\ln3\), integrate from 0:

\[F(x)=\frac3{20}\left[2e^{u/2}-4e^{-u/2}\right]_0^x =\frac3{10}\left(e^{x/2}-2e^{-x/2}+1\right).\]

The complete CDF has value 0 below 0 and 1 above \(2\ln3\). Substitution at the upper endpoint gives \((3/10)(3-2/3+1)=1\).

(b)

The transformation \(Y=e^{\frac{X}{2}}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(1\le Y\le3\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\le2 \ln{\left(y \right)})=F(2 \ln{\left(y \right)}).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt 1\\\frac{3 \left(y \left(y + 1\right) - 2\right)}{10 y},&1\le y\lt 3\\1,&y\ge 3.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{3 \left(1 + \frac{2}{y^{2}}\right)}{10},&1\le y\le 3\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.

(c)

For \(1\le y\le3\),

\[G(y)=\frac3{10}\left(y-\frac2y+1\right).\]

Set \(G(q)=3/5\). Then \(q-2/q+1=2\), so

\[q^2-q-2=(q-2)(q+1)=0.\]

Only \(q=2\) is in the support.

(d)

Using the transformed density,

\[\mathrm E(Y^4)=\frac3{10}\int_1^3\left(y^4+2y^2\right)dy =\frac3{10}\left[\frac{y^5}{5}+\frac{2y^3}{3}\right]_1^3.\]

Thus

\[\mathrm E(Y^4)=\frac3{10}\left(\frac{242}{5}+\frac{52}{3}\right)=\frac{493}{25}.\]
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Keep the negative sign in the antiderivative of the decaying exponential.

(b)

Use \(X\le2\ln y\), and map both support endpoints.

(c)

Convert the percentile equation into a quadratic.

(d)

Multiply g(y) by y to the fourth power, then integrate over the Y-support.

questions.title: A cube root giving a linear density
questions.prompt_html:
The random variable \(X\) has density

\[f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac16\left(2x^{-1/3}-x^{-2/3}\right),&1\le x\le8,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

  1. Find the cumulative distribution function of \(X\).

    [3]

  2. Let \(Y=X^{1/3}\). Find the probability density function of \(Y\).

    [3]

  3. Find the exact median of \(Y\).

    [2]
questions.answer_html:
(a)

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 1\\\frac{\sqrt[3]{x} \left(\sqrt[3]{x} - 1\right)}{2},&1\le x\lt 8\\1,&x\ge 8.\end{cases}\]

(b)

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}y - \frac{1}{2},&1\le y\le 2\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

(c)

\[\frac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Integrate from the lower support endpoint for \(1\le x\lt 8\):

\[F(x)=0+\int_{1}^{x}\frac{2 - \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{u}}}{6 \sqrt[3]{u}}\,du=0+\left[\frac{\sqrt[3]{u} \left(\sqrt[3]{u} - 1\right)}{2}\right]_{1}^{x}=\frac{\sqrt[3]{x} \left(\sqrt[3]{x} - 1\right)}{2}\]

Outside the support the CDF is 0 below the lower endpoint and 1 above the upper endpoint. Hence

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 1\\\frac{\sqrt[3]{x} \left(\sqrt[3]{x} - 1\right)}{2},&1\le x\lt 8\\1,&x\ge 8.\end{cases}\]

The pieces meet continuously, and the CDF is non-decreasing from 0 to 1.

(b)

The transformation \(Y=\sqrt[3]{X}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(1\le Y\le2\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\ley^{3})=F(y^{3}).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt 1\\\frac{y \left(y - 1\right)}{2},&1\le y\lt 2\\1,&y\ge 2.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}y - \frac{1}{2},&1\le y\le 2\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.

(c)

The CDF in the support is \(G(y)=(y^2-y)/2\). At the median,

\[m^2-m=1,\qquad m=\frac{1\pm\sqrt5}{2}.\]

Only the plus sign lies between 1 and 2. Hence

\[m=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}.\]
questions.hint_html:
(a)

The antiderivative can be written in terms of the first two powers of \(x^{1/3}\).

(b)

Use \(G(y)=F(y^3)\).

(c)

Choose the root in the transformed interval.

questions.title: A decreasing inverse square
questions.prompt_html:
The density of \(X\) is

\[f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac4{15}\left(1+\frac1{x^2}\right),&1\le x\le4,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

  1. Find \(\mathrm E(\sqrt X)\).

    [3]

  2. Let \(Y=1/X^2\). Find the probability density function of \(Y\).

    [4]

  3. Find the exact 40th percentile of \(Y\).

    [3]
questions.answer_html:
(a)

\[\frac{68}{45}.\]

(b)

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{2 \left(y + 1\right)}{15 y^{\frac{3}{2}}},&\frac{1}{16}\le y\le 1\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

(c)

\[\frac{\left(-9 + \sqrt{145}\right)^{2}}{64}\]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Integrate the function against the density:

\[\mathrm E(\sqrt X)=\frac4{15}\int_1^4\left(x^{1/2}+x^{-3/2}\right)dx =\frac4{15}\left[\frac23x^{3/2}-2x^{-1/2}\right]_1^4.\]

Therefore

\[\mathrm E(\sqrt X)=\frac4{15}\left(\frac{14}{3}+1\right)=\frac{68}{45}.\]

(b)

The transformation \(Y=\frac{1}{X^{2}}\) is decreasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(\frac{1}{16}\le Y\le1\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\ge\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}})=1-F(\frac{1}{\sqrt{y}}).\]

Because the transformation is decreasing, the inequality reverses. Since \(X\) is continuous, either endpoint convention gives the same tail probability.

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt \frac{1}{16}\\\frac{15 \sqrt{y} + 4 y - 4}{15 \sqrt{y}},&\frac{1}{16}\le y\lt 1\\1,&y\ge 1.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{2 \left(y + 1\right)}{15 y^{\frac{3}{2}}},&\frac{1}{16}\le y\le 1\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.

(c)

Let this percentile be \(q\). As \(G(q)=1-F(1/\sqrt q)\), the equation is

\[F(1/\sqrt q)=\frac35.\]

Put \(z=1/\sqrt q\). The CDF of \(X\) is \((4/15)(z-1/z)\), so

\[\frac4{15}\left(z-\frac1z\right)=\frac35 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad 4z^2-9z-4=0.\]

The admissible root is \(z=(9+\sqrt{145})/8\). Therefore

\[q=\frac1{z^2}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{145}-9}{8}\right)^2.\]

This value lies between \(1/16\) and 1. The 40th percentile of Y corresponds to the 60th percentile of X, not its 40th percentile.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Use the power rule on both terms after multiplication by \(\sqrt x\).

(b)

For positive X, \(1/X^2\le y\) means \(X\ge1/\sqrt y\).

(c)

Decreasing transformations swap lower and upper percentile probabilities.

\[5 \left(2 - \sqrt[3]{2}\right)\]

\[\frac{1300}{7}.\]

questions.prompt_html:

    [3]

  2. Find \(a\) such that \(\mathrm P(X\le a)=5/6\).

    [3]

  3. Let \(Y=\sqrt[3]{X+2}\). Find the probability density function of \(Y\), using its CDF.

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 0\\\frac{x}{6},&0\le x\lt 2\\1-\frac{(6-x)^2}{24},&2\le x\lt 6\\1,&x\ge 6.\end{cases}\]

(a)

Integrate from the lower support endpoint for \(0\le x\lt 2\):

\[F(x)=0+\int_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{6}\,du=0+\left[\frac{u}{6}\right]_{0}^{x}=\frac{x}{6}\]

\[F(x)=\frac{1}{3}+\int_{2}^{x}\frac{6 - u}{12}\,du=\frac{1}{3}+\left[\frac{u \left(12 - u\right)}{24}\right]_{2}^{x}=1-\frac{(6-x)^2}{24}\]

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 0\\\frac{x}{6},&0\le x\lt 2\\1-\frac{(6-x)^2}{24},&2\le x\lt 6\\1,&x\ge 6.\end{cases}\]

Because \(F(2)=1/3\lt5/6\), \(a\) lies in the second interval. Thus

\[1-\frac{(6-a)^2}{24}=\frac56 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (6-a)^2=4.\]

The algebraic possibilities are \(a=4\) and \(a=8\). Only \(a=4\) lies in \([2,6]\).

(c)

The transformation \(Y=\sqrt[3]{X + 2}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(\sqrt[3]{2}\le Y\le2\).

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\ley^{3} - 2)=F(y^{3} - 2).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt \sqrt[3]{2}\\\frac{y^{3} - 2}{6},&\sqrt[3]{2}\le y\lt \sqrt[3]4\\\frac{- y^{6} + 16 y^{3} - 40}{24},&\sqrt[3]4\le y\lt 2\\1,&y\ge 2.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{y^{2}}{2},&\sqrt[3]{2}\le y\lt \sqrt[3]4\\\frac{y^{2} \left(8 - y^{3}\right)}{4},&\sqrt[3]4\le y\le 2\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.

(a)

\[\frac{137}{40}.\]

(b)

Use both pieces:

\[\mathrm E(X)=\frac3{32}\int_0^4(3x-x^{3/2})dx+\frac3{16}\int_4^9x^{1/2}dx.\]
\[=\frac3{32}\left[\frac{3x^2}{2}-\frac25x^{5/2}\right]_0^4+ \frac3{16}\left[\frac23x^{3/2}\right]_4^9 =\frac{21}{20}+\frac{19}{8}=\frac{137}{40}.\]

(b)

The transformation \(Y=\sqrt{X}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(0\le Y\le3\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\ley^{2})=F(y^{2}).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt 0\\\frac{y^{2} \left(9 - 2 y\right)}{32},&0\le y\lt 2\\\frac{3 y - 1}{8},&2\le y\lt 3\\1,&y\ge 3.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{3 y \left(3 - y\right)}{16},&0\le y\lt 2\\\frac{3}{8},&2\le y\le 3\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.

The transformed density is \(3y(3-y)/16\) below 2 and \(3/8\) from 2 to 3. Both pieces have height \(3/8\) at the join.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Multiply each piece by x before integrating.

(b)

The old join at 4 becomes a join at 2.

questions.title: Quartiles before a shifted square root
questions.prompt_html:
The CDF of \(X\) is

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt0,\\\frac{15x-x^2}{50},&0\le x\lt5,\\1,&x\ge5.\end{cases}\]

  1. Find the exact interquartile range of \(X\).

    [4]

  2. Find \(\mathrm E(X^3)\).

    [3]

  3. Let \(Y=\sqrt{X+4}\). Find its probability density function.

    [4]
questions.answer_html:
(a)

\[\frac52\left(\sqrt7-\sqrt3\right)\]

(b)

\[\frac{175}{8}.\]

(c)

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{y \left(23 - 2 y^{2}\right)}{25},&2\le y\le 3\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

For a percentile probability \(p\), solve \((15q-q^2)/50=p\). The root in \([0,5]\) is

\[q=\frac{15-\sqrt{225-200p}}2.\]

Therefore

\[Q_1=\frac{15-5\sqrt7}{2},\qquad Q_3=\frac{15-5\sqrt3}{2}.\]

The plus-sign quadratic roots exceed 5 and are inadmissible. Hence

\[\mathrm{IQR}=\frac52(\sqrt7-\sqrt3).\]

(b)

The density is \(f(x)=(15-2x)/50\) for \(0\le x\le5\). Thus

\[\mathrm E(X^3)=\frac1{50}\int_0^5(15x^3-2x^4)dx =\frac1{50}\left[\frac{15x^4}{4}-\frac{2x^5}{5}\right]_0^5=\frac{175}{8}.\]

(c)

The transformation \(Y=\sqrt{X + 4}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(2\le Y\le3\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\ley^{2} - 4)=F(y^{2} - 4).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt 2\\\frac{- y^{4} + 23 y^{2} - 76}{50},&2\le y\lt 3\\1,&y\ge 3.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{y \left(23 - 2 y^{2}\right)}{25},&2\le y\le 3\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Keep the quadratic root that lies in the support.

(b)

Differentiate F, then use the third-moment integral.

(c)

The inverse is \(X=Y^2-4\), and the new support is not \([0,\sqrt5]\).

questions.title: Fractional moments before a shifted cube
questions.prompt_html:
The CDF of \(X\) is

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt3,\\\frac{x^2-9}{72},&3\le x\lt9,\\1,&x\ge9.\end{cases}\]

  1. Find \(\mathrm P(4\le X\le7)\).

    [2]

  2. Find \(\mathrm E(\sqrt X)\).

    [2]

  3. Find \(\operatorname{Var}(\sqrt X)\).

    [2]

  4. Let \(Y=(X-1)^3\). Find its probability density function.

    [3]
questions.answer_html:
(a)

\[\frac{11}{24}.\]

(b)

\[\frac{27-\sqrt3}{10}.\]

(c)

\[\frac{27\sqrt3-41}{50}.\]

(d)

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{\sqrt[3]{y} + 1}{108 y^{\frac{2}{3}}},&8\le y\le 512\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Subtract the two CDF values:

\[F(7)-F(4)=\frac{49-9}{72}-\frac{16-9}{72}=\frac{33}{72}=\frac{11}{24}.\]

(b)

The density is \(f(x)=x/36\), so

\[\mathrm E(\sqrt X)=\frac1{36}\int_3^9x^{3/2}dx =\frac1{90}\left(9^{5/2}-3^{5/2}\right)=\frac{27-\sqrt3}{10}.\]

(c)

The second moment of \(\sqrt X\) is

\[\mathrm E(X)=\frac1{36}\int_3^9x^2dx=\frac{13}{2}.\]

Therefore

\[\operatorname{Var}(\sqrt X)=\frac{13}{2}-\left(\frac{27-\sqrt3}{10}\right)^2 =\frac{27\sqrt3-41}{50}.\]

(d)

The transformation \(Y=\left(X - 1\right)^{3}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(8\le Y\le512\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\le\sqrt[3]{y} + 1)=F(\sqrt[3]{y} + 1).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt 8\\\frac{y^{\frac{2}{3}} + 2 \sqrt[3]{y} - 8}{72},&8\le y\lt 512\\1,&y\ge 512.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{\sqrt[3]{y} + 1}{108 y^{\frac{2}{3}}},&8\le y\le 512\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Both limits lie inside the same CDF branch.

(b)

Use \(\sqrt x\,f(x)\).

(c)

Use \(\mathrm E(X)\) as the second moment of the square-root variable.

(d)

Map the original endpoints through the shifted cube.

questions.title: A logarithmic transformation
questions.prompt_html:
The random variable \(X\) has density

\[f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac3{56}(x+1)^2,&1\le x\le3,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

  1. Find the cumulative distribution function of \(X\).

    [2]

  2. Let \(Y=\ln(X+1)\). Find its probability density function.

    [3]

  3. Find the exact median of \(Y\).

    [2]

  4. Find \(\mathrm E(Y)\) exactly.

    [3]
questions.answer_html:
(a)

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 1\\\frac{(x+1)^3-8}{56},&1\le x\lt 3\\1,&x\ge 3.\end{cases}\]

(b)

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{3 e^{3 y}}{56},&\ln{\left(2 \right)}\le y\le \ln{\left(4 \right)}\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

(c)

\[\frac13\ln36.\]

(d)

\[\frac{15}{7}\ln2-\frac13.\]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Integrate from the lower support endpoint for \(1\le x\lt 3\):

\[F(x)=0+\int_{1}^{x}\frac{3 \left(u + 1\right)^{2}}{56}\,du=0+\left[\frac{u \left(u^{2} + 3 u + 3\right)}{56}\right]_{1}^{x}=\frac{(x+1)^3-8}{56}\]

Outside the support the CDF is 0 below the lower endpoint and 1 above the upper endpoint. Hence

\[F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x\lt 1\\\frac{(x+1)^3-8}{56},&1\le x\lt 3\\1,&x\ge 3.\end{cases}\]

The pieces meet continuously, and the CDF is non-decreasing from 0 to 1.

(b)

The transformation \(Y=\ln{\left(X + 1 \right)}\) is increasing on the support of \(X\). Mapping the endpoints gives \(\ln{\left(2 \right)}\le Y\le\ln{\left(4 \right)}\).

For \(y\) within this range,

\[G(y)=\mathrm P(Y\le y)=\mathrm P(X\lee^{y} - 1)=F(e^{y} - 1).\]

Substituting separately into the appropriate branches of the original CDF gives

\[G(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\lt \ln{\left(2 \right)}\\\frac{e^{3 y} - 8}{56},&\ln{\left(2 \right)}\le y\lt \ln{\left(4 \right)}\\1,&y\ge \ln{\left(4 \right)}.\end{cases}\]

Differentiate each non-constant branch with respect to \(y\):

\[g(y)=\begin{cases}\frac{3 e^{3 y}}{56},&\ln{\left(2 \right)}\le y\le \ln{\left(4 \right)}\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]

The density is zero elsewhere. Values assigned to a density at isolated endpoints do not affect probabilities.

(c)

For \(\ln2\le y\le\ln4\), the CDF is \(G(y)=(e^{3y}-8)/56\). Set it equal to \(1/2\):

\[e^{3m}-8=28,\qquad e^{3m}=36,\qquad m=\frac13\ln36.\]

The value lies between \(\ln2\) and \(\ln4\).

(d)

The transformed density is \(g(y)=3e^{3y}/56\). Integrate by parts:

\[\mathrm E(Y)=\frac3{56}\int_{\ln2}^{\ln4}ye^{3y}dy =\frac1{56}\left[e^{3y}\left(y-\frac13\right)\right]_{\ln2}^{\ln4}.\]

Use \(e^{3\ln4}=64\), \(e^{3\ln2}=8\), and \(\ln4=2\ln2\):

\[\mathrm E(Y)=\frac{64(\ln4-1/3)-8(\ln2-1/3)}{56} =\frac{15}{7}\ln2-\frac13.\]

As a check, this result lies inside the support interval of Y.
questions.hint_html:
(a)

Use the antiderivative \((x+1)^3/56\), then subtract its value at 1.

(b)

The inverse is \(X=e^Y-1\).

(c)

Use the transformed CDF and take a natural logarithm.

(d)

Use integration by parts on \(ye^{3y}\).
